one_liner: GPL-3.0 add-on for Little CMS 2 that swaps stock transforms for precomputed-table, SSE2 and 15-bit kernels; about 7x on one Lab-to-RGB float case.
what_it_does: An optional plugin, built from plugins/fast_float inside the lcms2 repo (configure --with-fastfloat, meson -Dfastfloat=true), that you enable with one call: cmsPlugin(cmsFastFloatExtensions()). After that, cmsCreateTransform() asks the plugin's dispatcher first, and it replaces the transform with a specialised kernel when the formats and pipeline match. It also adds Photoshop-style 1.15 fixed-point formats (TYPE_RGB_15 and others) and dithered 8-bit output formats (TYPE_RGB_8_DITHER and others). The API is unchanged: the same lcms2 calls run faster when a kernel matches and fall back to stock lcms2 when none does.
how_it_is_fast: At transform creation the dispatcher tries, in order, 15-bit matrix-shaper, joined 8-bit curves, an SSE2 8-bit matrix-shaper (float matrix on 1.14 fixed-point shaper tables, chosen after a runtime cpuid check), a plain 8-bit matrix-shaper, joined float curves, a float matrix-shaper, 8-bit and 16-bit prelinearization plus tetrahedral CLUT, and float CLUTs for RGB, CMYK and Lab input. The float Lab-input path (fast_float_lab.c) resamples the whole Lab-to-device pipeline into a 51^3 float grid (33 with cmsFLAGS_LOWRESPRECALC, 66 with HIGHRESPRECALC), puts a sigmoid on the a*/b* axes, and evaluates each pixel with tetrahedral interpolation. Stock lcms2 instead runs every float pipeline stage per pixel (its own optimizers skip float formats). So the speedup comes from replacing exact evaluation with table lookups, not only from SIMD.
when_to_use: You already use lcms2 and run float-to-float transforms (Gray, RGB, CMYK or Lab input) on large images, e.g. a raw developer's working-space-to-output step.
8-bit RGB or CMYK transforms on whole images, where the precomputed curve, matrix and tetrahedral tables pay off over millions of pixels.
Pipelines that hold Photoshop 1.15 fixed-point data (TYPE_*_15) or need dithered 8-bit output to reduce banding.
Your application is GPL-3.0-compatible, or you will buy the commercial licence the plugin PDF offers.
You want speed and keep full ICC v4 profile support: profile parsing and pipeline construction are still done by lcms2.
when_not_to_use: Closed-source or MIT-only products that cannot accept GPL-3.0-or-later and will not buy the alternate licence. The lcms2 core is MIT; this plugin is not.

Workflows that need bit-identical output to stock lcms2. The testbed accepts float differences up to 0.005 (EPSILON_FLOAT_TESTS) and 0.007 in another check. For the Lab float path, CheckLab2RGB only prints the maximum RGB distance and asserts no limit.
Soft-proofing or gamut-check transforms (the dispatcher refuses cmsFLAGS_SOFTPROOFING), reversed-polarity (FLAVOR) formats, or transforms that later need cmsChangeBuffersFormat().

Small per-call batches, e.g. one pixel per call or per-scanline calls. The PDF says creating the transform and starting a call are costly, and it recommends one cmsDoTransformLineStride() call over many lines.
Unbounded or out-of-range float Lab input. The Lab kernel clamps L* to 0..100 and a*/b* to -128..128 before indexing the grid.

integration.form: static or shared lib (liblcms2_fast_float), built from the plugins/fast_float directory of the lcms2 source tree; off by default in autotools, meson and CMake
integration.min_toolchain: C99 compiler (also compiles as C++ since 2.12); autotools, meson or CMake 3.16+; Visual Studio project in plugins/fast_float/VC2022
integration.platforms: Any platform lcms2 supports. The SSE2 8-bit matrix-shaper kernel is x86 only, with runtime detection, and CMS_DONT_USE_SSE2 disables it. Every other kernel is portable scalar C, and there are no NEON or AVX kernels.
integration.thread_safety: Transforms evaluate read-only tables built at creation time. Register the plugin once at startup, globally with cmsPlugin or per context with cmsPluginTHR. Beyond that, the plugin's threading is not documented.
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial: one registration call and no other API change, but transforms created with cmsFLAGS_NOOPTIMIZE never reach the plugin (lcms2 2.11+ skips transform plugins under that flag), outputs differ slightly from stock, and only matching format and colour-space combinations are accelerated

gotchas: cmsFLAGS_NOOPTIMIZE silently disables the plugin. In lcms2 2.11, 2.12 and current master, AllocEmptyTransform calls transform plugins only when that flag is clear, and the plugin PDF does not mention this. RawTherapee's current lab2rgbOut creates its Lab_FLT-to-RGB_FLT transform with cmsFLAGS_NOOPTIMIZE | cmsFLAGS_NOCACHE.

The autotools build compiles the plugin with -Ofast (plugins/fast_float/src/Makefile.am). That flag implies -ffast-math, under which the isnan() guards in fclamp, flerp and fclamp128 may be optimised away. The meson build does not add -Ofast.

Past wrong-output and crash bugs in the plugin's issue history, all closed now: #272 (8-bit RGB to Lab with Optimize8BitRGBTransform), #325 (float sRGB to Lab off by about 100x in 2.13.1), #247 (Krita, broken or transparent tiles with cLUT display profiles), #236 and #260 (segfaults). Test your own profiles against stock lcms2 before switching.
On aarch64 nothing is vectorised. PR #549 (March 2026) fixed an ARM64 compile failure in the SSE2 file, so older releases may not build there.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over moxcms (Rust) or jsColorEngine (JS/WASM) when you are in C or C++, already depend on lcms2's full ICC v4.4 implementation, and want the speedup without changing your colour-management code. Pick babl only inside GEGL/GIMP. moxcms publishes reproducible numbers against lcms2, while this plugin has only one anecdotal number.
verified_claims_summary: One RawTherapee developer (issue #6016, Dec 2020) reported that the Lab-to-RGB output transform for a 45.6 MP export took 5312 ms with stock lcms2 and 754 ms with the plugin (about 7x). No CPU, thread count, compiler, flags or lcms2 commit are given. lcms2 since 2.11 skips plugins under cmsFLAGS_NOOPTIMIZE, which RawTherapee's lab2rgbOut still passes, so that run must have used locally modified RawTherapee code that was not published on the issue page as read here. The fast path for that case is the 51^3 tetrahedral Lab grid, an approximation of stock output whose error the testbed reports but does not bound.
status_note: Actively maintained in the lcms2 repo (last commit 2026-10-02; the ChangeLog says the formerly commercial plugin was open-sourced under GPL3 in 2.10). It is copyable under GPL-3.0-or-later or a paid licence, while the lcms2 core stays MIT. Correction to the record: RawTherapee does not ship it. Issue #6016 is still open, and RawTherapee's dev CMakeLists.txt, rtengine/iccstore.cc, rtengine/init.cc and rtgui/main.cc never call cmsFastFloatExtensions.
